name: David Sacks

summary.text: David O. Sacks, born in Cape Town and raised in Tennessee, earned a Stanford economics B.A. in 1994. He was editor-in-chief of The Stanford Review, the paper Peter Thiel co-founded, and co-wrote The Diversity Myth (1995) with Thiel; in 2016 both apologized for parts of the book. After a University of Chicago J.D. (1998), he spent January to November 1999 at McKinsey, working on telecommunications and financial services clients. He has said Thiel called him there to tell him about Confinity. He joined in November 1999 and ran product (most recently as Executive Vice President of Product). PayPal's filings name him Chief Operating Officer from February 2002. Apart from the McKinsey client work, no public record was found of pre-1999 government, intelligence or finance-industry roles.

facts.claim: Sacks was born in Cape Town, South Africa, in 1972; his family moved to Tennessee when he was five.

sources.title: Meet David Sacks, member of the 'PayPal Mafia' and Trump crypto czar

facts.claim: Sacks received a B.A. in Economics from Stanford University in 1994 and a J.D. from the University of Chicago Law School in 1998.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form 10-K405 for fiscal year 2001

facts.claim: Sacks was editor-in-chief of The Stanford Review as a student. In a 2010 interview quoted by the paper, he said it made the outside world more aware of what was happening at Stanford.
facts.quote: I certainly think it made the outside world much more aware of what was happening at Stanford.

sources.title: A Brief and Non-Exhaustive History of The Stanford Review

facts.claim: Sacks and Thiel co-wrote 'The Diversity Myth: Multiculturalism and Political Intolerance on Campus', published in 1995 by the Independent Institute, a Bay Area think tank.

sources.title: The Making of Peter Thiel's Networks

facts.claim: In September 1996 Sacks and Thiel published 'The Case Against Affirmative Action' in Stanford Magazine. The byline described Sacks as a law student at the University of Chicago and Thiel as someone who 'runs an investment firm'.
facts.quote: David Sacks, '94, is a law student at the University of Chicago.

sources.title: The Case Against Affirmative Action

facts.claim: Sacks worked as a management consultant for McKinsey & Company from January 1999 to November 1999, focusing on the telecommunications and financial services industries.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form 10-K405 for fiscal year 2001

facts.claim: Sacks said Thiel called him at McKinsey about Confinity's PalmPilot money-beaming product, which he thought was a dumb idea. He said he agreed to quit McKinsey once the company moved to sending money by email.
facts.quote: I thought it was a dumb idea.

sources.title: Lessons of Greatness: Start a Movement; not just a business

facts.claim: Sacks joined PayPal (then Confinity) in November 1999 and held several posts, most recently Executive Vice President of Product, before becoming Chief Operating Officer in February 2002.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form 10-K405 for fiscal year 2001

facts.claim: In July 2001 PayPal lent Sacks $450,000 under its non-recourse employee liquidity program. In September 2001 the company bought back part of participants' shares at $3 per share, and the proceeds repaid the loans.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form 10-K405 for fiscal year 2001

facts.claim: In January 2002 Sacks transferred his PayPal shares to DS PPI LLC, which he beneficially owns. On January 18, 2002 PayPal granted him an option to buy 325,118 shares.

sources.title: PayPal, Inc. Form 10-K405 for fiscal year 2001

facts.claim: In 2016 Sacks and Thiel both apologized for parts of The Diversity Myth.
facts.quote: I'm embarrassed by some of my former views and regret writing them.

sources.title: Meet David Sacks, member of the 'PayPal Mafia' and Trump crypto czar

facts.claim: When eBay agreed to buy PayPal in 2002, Sacks beneficially owned 278,674 PayPal shares (under 1% of 61.5 million outstanding) as of August 23, 2002, held through DS PPI LLC. He also held a January 2002 option on 325,118 shares, none exercisable within 60 days. The filing listed 63,999 restricted shares and 90,980 option shares that would accelerate on the merger. Each PayPal share converted into 0.39 eBay shares.

sources.title: eBay Inc. Amendment No. 1 to Form S-4 (PayPal merger proxy statement/prospectus)

facts.claim: The merger filing lists Sacks among executives (with Thiel, Levchin, Musk, Hoffman, Botha and others) who agreed to vote their PayPal shares, about 27.7% in total, for the eBay deal and accepted transfer restrictions. It also lists him among executives who signed eBay employment agreements; his was a 12-month term as PayPal's Chief Operating Officer.

sources.title: eBay Inc. Amendment No. 1 to Form S-4 (PayPal merger proxy statement/prospectus)

facts.claim: After eBay's 2002 purchase of PayPal, Sacks set up Room 9 Entertainment, which produced and financed the film 'Thank You for Smoking' (2005). TechCrunch put the eBay deal at $1.5 billion.

sources.title: PayPal, Pulp Fiction and Geni
Meet David Sacks, member of the 'PayPal Mafia' and Trump crypto czar

facts.claim: Sacks founded the genealogy site Geni in June 2006. It raised $16.5 million from Founders Fund and Charles River Ventures. Yammer was developed inside Geni. Sacks stepped down as Geni CEO in 2011, and MyHeritage bought Geni in November 2012 in what TechCrunch, citing MyHeritage investor Index, called an eight-figure cash-and-equity deal. Sacks joined MyHeritage's board.

sources.title: MyHeritage acquires Geni and $25M to build family tree of the whole world
All In The Family: MyHeritage Buys Former Yammer Stablemate Geni.com In An 8-Figure Deal, Raises $25M
PayPal, Pulp Fiction and Geni

facts.claim: Yammer, launched in 2008, raised an $85 million round led by DFJ Growth in February 2012. Earlier backers named in the report were Founders Fund, Charles River Ventures, Emergence Capital, Social+Capital Partnership and U.S. Venture Partners; individuals included Max Levchin and Bill Lee. The company had raised $142 million in total and did not disclose its valuation.

sources.title: Yammer closes $85M round, new desktop apps planned

facts.claim: Microsoft confirmed on June 25, 2012 that it would acquire Yammer for $1.2 billion in cash, with Sacks staying on as Yammer's CEO inside Microsoft's Office division. No public record was found of the size of Sacks's personal stake or proceeds.

sources.title: With $1.2 Billion Yammer Buy, Microsoft's Social Enterprise Strategy Takes Shape

facts.claim: On February 8, 2016 Zenefits founder Parker Conrad resigned as CEO amid regulatory problems over unlicensed insurance sales. Sacks, then chief operating officer, replaced him. In a staff memo he wrote that compliance processes and controls had been inadequate.
facts.quote: many of our internal processes, controls, and actions around compliance have been inadequate, and some decisions have just been plain wrong.

sources.title: Zenefits CEO Steps Down Over Regulatory Problems

facts.claim: In October 2017 Zenefits and Parker Conrad settled SEC charges, without admitting or denying the findings, that they misled investors in 2014 and 2015 private placements raising more than $565 million. The SEC said investors were not told about Conrad's licensing-course 'macro' or about unlicensed sales. Zenefits paid $450,000, a penalty the SEC capped for cooperation. Conrad paid $533,692. The order does not name Sacks, who had led the company in 2016 and then handed over to Jay Fulcher.

sources.title: In the Matter of YourPeople, Inc., dba Zenefits FTW Insurance Services and Parker Conrad (Release No. 33-10429)
SEC fines Zenefits and former CEO Parker Conrad nearly $1 million for misleading investors

facts.claim: Craft Ventures, co-founded in 2017 by Sacks and Bill Lee, raised a $350 million debut fund and closed a $500 million second fund in October 2019. In August 2021 it closed Craft Ventures III ($612 million) and Growth I ($510 million). In November 2023 it closed Craft Ventures IV ($712 million) and Growth II ($608 million), bringing assets under management to $3.3 billion.

sources.title: David Sacks's Craft Ventures just closed its second fund with $500 million
Craft Ventures collects $612m for third fund and $510m for debut growth fund

facts.claim: Few Craft limited partners are public. Venture Capital Journal reported that the Teachers' Retirement System of the State of Illinois committed $30 million each to Craft Ventures IV and Craft Ventures Growth II. No public record was found of other named LPs.

sources.title: David Sacks' Craft Ventures raises more than $1.6bn

facts.claim: Sacks invested in crypto custodian BitGo's $42.5 million round led by Valor Equity Partners in December 2017 and joined its board. In February 2020 Craft Ventures led a $10 million Series A for Bitcoin Lightning Network developer Lightning Labs. Insurance Journal's December 2024 report also named Bitwise among Craft's crypto investments.

facts.claim: Sacks co-hosted the All-In podcast, started in 2020, with Chamath Palihapitiya (Social Capital), Jason Calacanis and David Friedberg (The Production Board).

facts.claim: Sacks gave $70,223 to Ron DeSantis in 2021 and, in April 2022, $1 million to Protect Ohio Values PAC, a super PAC backing JD Vance's Senate bid, according to The New Republic as summarised by SFist; CBS News, citing FEC records, also reports the $1 million gift and that Peter Thiel gave the PAC $15 million. On September 15, 2022 Sacks co-hosted a Republican fundraiser with Keith Rabois whose reported guests included Vance, Blake Masters and Mehmet Oz.

sources.title: Wealthy SF recall backer pumping millions to DeSantis and J.D. Vance
The billionaire who fueled JD Vance's rapid rise to the Trump VP spot

facts.claim: In August 2022 Sacks asked the Delaware Chancery Court to quash Twitter's subpoenas to Craft Ventures Management LP and Sacks.com LLC in Twitter's suit to make Musk complete the $44 billion buyout. His lawyers argued that duplicate subpoenas in Delaware and California placed an 'unreasonable burden' on the firms and showed a 'harassing nature and intent,' Fortune reported.

sources.title: A member of Elon Musk's 'PayPal Mafia' says in court that Twitter is harassing his companies

facts.claim: After Musk took over Twitter in October 2022, Sacks joined Jason Calacanis and Sriram Krishnan in an informal advisory group. Sacks discussed ideas with the product team and was added to the company's internal Slack. On November 7 he tweeted that he had 'no official role'.

sources.title: Musk's Twitter fix-it team fades out as billionaire says transition is almost done

facts.claim: On May 24, 2023 Sacks moderated the Twitter Spaces event with Elon Musk where Ron DeSantis launched his 2024 presidential campaign. After technical failures the audio feed moved to Sacks's account.

sources.title: Twitter promises to 'keep experimenting' with Spaces—even after Ron DeSantis' glitchy campaign kick off

facts.claim: On June 6, 2024 Sacks and Chamath Palihapitiya hosted a Trump fundraiser at Sacks's San Francisco home. Tickets ran from $50,000 to $500,000 per couple. Fox News reported that it raised roughly $12 million. Sources told Fox News that Sacks said the event began with JD Vance asking him to host it.
facts.quote: this all started with JD Vance calling and asking if we could host an event for President Trump.

sources.title: Trump lands endorsement of top investor who hosted $12 million San Francisco fundraiser for former president

facts.claim: Sacks spoke on the first night of the Republican National Convention on July 15, 2024. Axios reported, as summarized by The Daily Beast, that Sacks, Musk and Tucker Carlson lobbied Trump that weekend to pick JD Vance as his running mate.

sources.title: VC David Sacks delivers a fire-and-brimstone speech at the Republican National Convention
Elon Musk and Tucker Carlson 'Secretly Lobbied' for Vance

facts.claim: On December 5, 2024 Trump named Sacks 'White House A.I. & Crypto Czar', saying he would work on a crypto legal framework and lead PCAST. A Craft spokeswoman said Sacks would not leave the firm. Business Insider noted that as a special government employee he need not divest or publicly disclose assets, could serve up to 130 days a year, and must recuse from matters affecting his holdings.

sources.title: Trump Names David Sacks as White House AI and Crypto Czar
Meet David Sacks, member of the 'PayPal Mafia' and Trump crypto czar

facts.claim: Executive Order 14178 (January 23, 2025) created the President's Working Group on Digital Asset Markets within the National Economic Council. It is chaired by the Special Advisor for AI and Crypto, Sacks's post, and was tasked with proposing a crypto regulatory framework and evaluating a 'national digital asset stockpile'.

sources.title: Executive Order 14178: Strengthening American Leadership in Digital Financial Technology

facts.claim: A March 5, 2025 waiver signed by White House Counsel David Warrington let Sacks, a special government employee, take part in digital-asset policy matters despite remaining holdings. The memo says he and Craft divested over $200 million of crypto-related positions, at least $85 million directly attributable to him. His remaining interests are crypto-company stakes held through Craft funds, which combined are under 3.8% of his total investment assets; the two largest, BitGo and Lightning Labs, are under 2.5% and 1.2% respectively.

sources.title: Memorandum for David O. Sacks: Limited Waiver Pursuant to 18 U.S.C. § 208(b)(1)
Trump Issues Ethics Waiver For His AI/Crypto Czar

facts.claim: The waiver memo lists the divestments: he and Craft sold all liquid cryptocurrency, including Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana, before January 20, 2025, and he sold his Bitwise 10 Crypto Index Fund position on January 22. He sold his Coinbase and Robinhood stock and sold, or began selling, his shares in private digital-asset companies. He sold LP interests in Multicoin Capital and Blockchain Capital, and Craft sold its interests in Multicoin Capital and Bitwise Asset Management. He also began selling his LP interests in Sequoia funds and about 90 other venture funds as a precaution.

sources.title: Memorandum for David O. Sacks: Limited Waiver Pursuant to 18 U.S.C. § 208(b)(1)
White House Crypto Czar David Sacks Confirms He Sold Digital Assets Before Taking Role

facts.claim: A second waiver covering AI matters, issued in mid-2025 (VKTR dates it to June; Nextgov to July), said Sacks had sold or arranged to sell direct AI interests including Amazon, Meta and TSMC, and more than 97% of affected Craft fund holdings, and that he, Craft and his family agreed not to directly acquire new interests in directly affected companies. Craft also agreed to consult White House Counsel before new investments. In July 2025 Vultron, an AI startup for federal contractors, announced a $22 million round that Craft backed. VKTR said it was unclear whether Craft consulted counsel or whether the deal conflicted with the waiver. The White House did not comment.

sources.title: Did AI Czar David Sacks Really Divest? New AI Investment Raises Ethics Questions
Democrats launch ethics investigation into AI and crypto czar David Sacks

facts.claim: At the July 18, 2025 GENIUS Act signing, Sacks said Trump 'stepped in and saved this bill.' The stablecoin law passed the House with 308 votes. On July 23, 2025 All-In and the Hill and Valley Forum co-hosted the 'Winning the AI Race' summit in Washington, with Vance and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as guests, while Sacks was serving as AI czar.

sources.title: Trump signs landmark GENIUS Act, hailing 'exciting new frontier' for crypto

facts.claim: On September 17, 2025 Sen. Elizabeth Warren, Rep. Melanie Stansbury and six other members of Congress opened an inquiry into whether Sacks had exceeded the 130-day limit for special government employees. They noted he remained a Craft Ventures general partner and that the number of days he had worked was not public.

sources.title: Warren, Stansbury, Members of Congress Launch Investigation into Trump Crypto & AI Czar's Ethics Conflicts
Democrats launch ethics investigation into AI and crypto czar David Sacks

facts.claim: A New York Times investigation, as summarized by TechCrunch, reported that 449 of Sacks's 708 tech investments involve AI and that his filings don't show the remaining values or sale dates of divested holdings. It also reported that All-In sought $1 million sponsorships tied to the July 2025 White House AI summit. Sacks called the story a 'nothing burger', and a spokesperson said the conflict-of-interest narrative was false. His lawyers said the event lost money and offered no access to Trump. NPR reported that Sacks and Craft Ventures maintain more than 400 investments in tech firms with ties to AI.

sources.title: New report examines how David Sacks might profit from Trump administration role
Trump tech adviser David Sacks under fire over vast AI investments

facts.claim: Sacks said in December 2025 that serving 'has actually cost me a lot of money' and that the OGE had approved his waivers. Ethics professor Kathleen Clark called them 'sham ethics waivers.' He pushed for a single national AI framework over state laws, and Trump signed an order directing the Justice Department to challenge 'onerous' state AI laws.

sources.title: Trump tech adviser David Sacks under fire over vast AI investments

facts.claim: On March 26–27, 2026 Sacks said he was leaving the AI and crypto czar post because he had used up his 130 days as a special government employee. He became co-chair of PCAST with OSTP director Michael Kratsios. In August 2026 a Form D showed Craft Ventures raising a fifth fund, reported at about $1 billion.
facts.quote: I had a role as a SGE [special government employee] that was 130 days

openQuestions: Exact years Sacks was Stanford Review editor-in-chief were not confirmed in a primary source.
Sources disagree on The Diversity Myth's date: The New Republic gives 1995, and a 1998 edition is also cited elsewhere. The publisher's page (independent.org) was behind a captcha and was not opened.
McKinsey's clients during Sacks's 1999 engagement are not public; the 10-K names only the industries (telecommunications and financial services).
No public record found of Sacks holding government or intelligence roles before 1999, or of outside investors backing him personally before PayPal.
Sacks's personal stake in and proceeds from the 2012 Yammer sale: no public figure found (Yammer was private).
Whether Sacks sold PayPal shares before the merger (e.g. in PayPal's 2002 secondary offering); the S-4/A shows only his holdings as of August 23, 2002.
The June/July 2025 AI ethics waiver memo itself was not located; its details here rest on VKTR and Nextgov reporting.
Craft Ventures' limited partners beyond Illinois TRS: an aggregator claim that the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and Saudi PIF are LPs could not be verified.

FEC primary records for the $1 million Protect Ohio Values contribution and for Purple Good Government PAC (Axios, March 2024, reported it was Sacks-funded and gave $93,400 to Bernie Moreno); the FEC API and Axios page were not reachable.

The original New York Times investigation (Nov. 30, 2025) could not be opened; claims here rely on TechCrunch's summary. Reported involvement in the 2025 UAE/G42 Nvidia chip arrangement is unverified.
Whether Sacks exceeded the 130-day SGE limit before March 2026: no public day count found.
Craft Ventures co-investments with Andreessen Horowitz: not confirmed from a primary source.
